content.text: I reviewed every input file, all ten draft sections, the numeral ledger, and all five figure briefs, and traced each limitation, numbered part, and figure statement to the disclosure text.

input.summary: Full ledger built and traced. All 17 claims (claims 1-10 apparatus, 11-13 installed assembly, 14-17 method) were traced limitation by limitation to affirmative disclosure passages: split frame halves with hinge at one end and releasable latch at the other; three radial jaw carriages in radial guides with pivoting concave jaw pads that avoid a tool-specific pipe diameter; outward-biasing carriage springs; a segmented cam ring in an annular guide with one segment per frame half; complementary drive faces at the hinge end and latch end that couple on closure; followers in respective oblique slots; a latch-carried wedge bearing on a drive face of the cam ring and rotating it through a limited stroke; the first holding position and the second over-center position; the force-limiting spring stack between latch handle and wedge that takes up remaining latch travel; the indicator pin moving relative to a fixed edge of the latch housing at a predetermined compression range and expressly not measuring pipe diameter; the mounting boss outside the annular guide that does not participate in jaw synchronization; and the install/remove sequences. All 28 numerals (10-66) were checked: each has one and only one meaning, each appears in the description, and each appears on at least one figure sheet; no orphan or duplicated numeral was found. All five figure briefs were checked against the disclosure and against the Brief Description of the Drawings; figure-to-figure geometry (hinge at the left break, latch at the right break, first frame half and first cam-ring segment upper, second frame half and second segment lower, three carriages/slots at top, lower left and lower right clear of both breaks) is mutually consistent, and no section line is designated anywhere so no section-designation mismatch arises. The drafting agent's assertion in the conversation about a "self-adhering layer with a microsuction surface" is agent prose, not inventor support, and correctly appears nowhere in the draft. No drafting note, placeholder, open question, unresolved alternative, or "by way of example"/"any closed outline" shape-justifying language remains in the application text. Two defects are reported: (1) FIG. 3 verbalizes an undisclosed circumferential position for the ring drive face (a functional drive surface) by requiring it to be drawn clear of the slot outlines and the junction end faces, which under the functional-surface rule is substantive geometry rather than a depiction convention and has no affirmative source; and (2) a number mismatch between claim 1's single "a carriage spring biasing each jaw carriage" and claim 9's "the carriage spring of each jaw carriage" (and claim 16's "a respective carriage spring"), which the disclosure resolves as one spring per carriage. Everything else in the description, summary, abstract, and figure briefs traced to an affirmative inventor passage; Background prior-art characterizations were left for the separate prior-art trace, and the brief's note that the supplied art may be incomplete is acknowledged.

findings.title: FIG. 3 brief verbalizes an undisclosed circumferential position for the ring drive face
findings.where: figures/FIG-3.md, "Geometry to draw" list, final bullet (and the related numeral target for 54)
findings.detail: The ring drive face 54 is a functional drive surface: the wedge 52 bears on it and rotates the coupled cam ring through the limited stroke. The brief does not merely give it a generic outline; it states where it sits circumferentially relative to two other functional features, i.e. away from all three oblique slots and away from the junction end faces at the hinge and latch ends. Under the functional-surface rule, a circumferential end position of a drive face is substantive even when the brief calls the geometry schematic. The disclosure says only "Closing the latch drives a wedge against a drive face of the cam ring and rotates the coupled ring through a limited stroke" and never says where on the ring that face lies; in particular it never says the face is spaced away from the latch-end junction, which is where the wedge acts. No affirmative USER passage anywhere in disclosure.md or the USER turn of conversation.md places the drive face relative to the slots or the segment end faces. The legibility rationale ("so that its lead line reads cleanly") does not convert a positional relationship into a permitted depiction convention, because the relationship is verbalized in the brief.
findings.evidence: Candidate wording (figures/FIG-3.md): "A short plain drive face on the band. The drive face is shown schematically, and is drawn clear of the three slot outlines and of the junction end faces so that its lead line reads cleanly." Nearest source passage (disclosure.md, paragraph 2), which shows the gap: "Closing the latch drives a wedge against a drive face of the cam ring and rotates the coupled ring through a limited stroke." — the source discloses the face and its function but no circumferential location, no spacing from the oblique slots, and no spacing from the hinge-end or latch-end drive faces.
findings.fix: Replace the bullet with a minimally specific, relationship-free statement: "- A short plain drive face on the band. The drive face is shown schematically; its outline and its position on the band are a depiction convention and are not stated to bear any relationship to the slot outlines or to the junction end faces." Keep the numeral target as "54: the short plain drive face on the band." Make no addition to the description, Brief Description of the Drawings, or claims to justify the chosen location.

findings.title: Claim 1 recites one carriage spring for all three carriages while claim 9 and claim 16 treat the springs as one per carriage
findings.where: draft/09-claims.md, claim 1 (fourth element), claim 9, claim 16; cf. draft/08-detailed-description.md, "Jaw carriages and jaw pads"
findings.detail: Claim 1 introduces "a carriage spring biasing each jaw carriage outward from the central axis," which on its literal reading is a single spring acting on all three carriages. Claim 9 then refers to "the carriage spring of each jaw carriage," and claim 16 recites "a respective carriage spring biasing each jaw carriage outward," both of which presuppose one spring per carriage. The description likewise uses the plural ("the carriage springs 42 retract the jaw carriages 22"), matching the disclosure. The claim set is therefore internally inconsistent in number and claim 9 lacks clean antecedent basis for a per-carriage spring.
findings.evidence: Claim 1: "a carriage spring biasing each jaw carriage outward from the central axis". Claim 9: "wherein the carriage spring of each jaw carriage retracts that jaw carriage outward". Description: "When the releasable latch 18 is released, the carriage springs 42 retract the jaw carriages 22 outward". Disclosure support for one per carriage: "A spring biases each carriage outward when the latch is released."
findings.fix: In claim 1, amend the element to read: "a respective carriage spring biasing each jaw carriage outward from the central axis;". Leave claims 9 and 16 and the description unchanged; the antecedent then matches both.
